legend: You are given a set S%%ZSMJ0%% of n%%ZSMJ1%% distinct integers. You will also receive q%%ZSMJ2%% queries, each of one of the following two types:
Query Type 1 (1x)%%ZSMJ3%%:   If x%%ZSMJ4%% is currently in the set S%%ZSMJ5%%, remove it.
Otherwise, add x%%ZSMJ6%% to the set.
Query Type 2 (2t)%%ZSMJ7%%:   Print the cumulative bitwise XOR of (x+t)%%ZSMJ8%% over all x∈S%%ZSMJ9%%. Formally, print ⨁x∈S(x+t)%%ZSMJ10%%.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n%%ZSMJ11%% and q%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤n,q≤3⋅105%%ZSMJ13%%) — the initial size of the set and the number of queries, respectively.
The next line of the input will contain n%%ZSMJ14%% distinct integers x1,x2⋯xn%%ZSMJ15%% (0≤xi<220%%ZSMJ16%%)  — the initial set.

The next q%%ZSMJ17%% lines of the input will describe the queries. Each of them will contain a query of the form 1x%%ZSMJ18%% or 2t%%ZSMJ19%% (0≤x,t<220%%ZSMJ20%%), representing the query in the format described above.
It is guaranteed that there is at least one query of type 2%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: For each query of type 2%%ZSMJ22%%, print the cumulative bitwise XOR of (x+t)%%ZSMJ23%% over all x∈S%%ZSMJ24%%.
note: In the sample case, at the time of the first type 2%%ZSMJ25%% query, we have S={1,6,15}%%ZSMJ26%%. Since t=0%%ZSMJ27%% for this query, we print the value (1+0)⊕(6+0)⊕(15+0)=1⊕6⊕15=8%%ZSMJ28%% At the time of the second type 2%%ZSMJ29%% query, we have S={1,5,10,15}%%ZSMJ30%%. Since t=3%%ZSMJ31%% for this query, we print the value (1+3)⊕(5+3)⊕(10+3)⊕(15+3)=4⊕8⊕13⊕18=19%%ZSMJ32%%
